bracket: [Textbook misprint, TWO of them, neither changing the value. (1) The stem says "the solenoid in Exercise 5.5", but Exercise 5.5 is a BAR MAGNET, not a solenoid — the intended target is Exercise 5.3. The book's own key proves it: Ex 5.3's solenoid has \(m = 0.60\,\text{J T}^{-1}\), which gives \(\tau = mB\sin\theta = 0.075\,\text{N m}\) — exactly the printed answer — while Ex 5.5's magnet (\(m = 1.5\)) would give \(0.1875\). A leftover from the pre-rationalisation numbering. (2) The key states that torque with the UNIT JOULE. Torque is measured in newton-metres; the key itself prints "N m" for the same quantity at Exercise 4.9 and "Nm" at 5.6(b). The magnitude \(7.5 \times 10^{-2}\) is correct.]

[Textbook misprint in the answer key (unit only): all four values agree with the answer below, but the key gives the torque in part (b)(i) as \(0.33\,\text{J}\). Torque is measured in newton-metres, not joules — the key prints "N m" correctly for the same quantity elsewhere. [Textbook defects in the book's own worked solution, THREE of them. (1) It states that "the field \(H\) is dependent of the material of the core" — the word INdependent is meant, which is the whole point of introducing \(H\). (2) The question asks for (a) \(H\), (b) \(M\), (c) \(B\), but the printed solution answers them in the order \(H\), \(B\), \(M\), so its own labels (b) and (c) are swapped. (3) It prints \(B = \mu_r n(I + I_M)\), which is dimensionally impossible since \(\mu_r\) is a pure number; only \(B = \mu_0 n(I + I_M)\) reproduces the book's own printed value.]
